references.text: Moses reminds the people that they were slaves in Egypt, which is the background for the warning about being sent back to Egypt by ship.
The Lord promised that the Israelites would never see the Egyptians again, making the threat of returning to Egypt all the more serious.
Describes a similar judgment where the people will waste away in enemy lands, parallel to the slavery mentioned in Deuteronomy 28:68.
The king was warned against leading the people back to Egypt, showing that this was an ongoing concern.
Hosea prophesies that Israel will return to Egypt because of their sin, fulfilling the warning in Deuteronomy.
The prophecy that Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean things in Assyria, linked to the curse in Deuteronomy.
Jeremiah warns that those who flee to Egypt to escape sword and famine will die there.
Joel describes how enemies sold Israel's children, reminiscent of being sold as slaves with no buyers.
Amos mentions that Israelites were sold, connecting to the slavery and sale described in the curse.
